name: Civitavecchia
title: Civitavecchia UTM | Cruise & Ferry Ship Thickness Gauging
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Civitavecchia for cruise ships, Sardinia ferries, ro-ro and bulk carriers: scrubber piping, hull and deck gauging.
h1: Thickness Gauging for Cruise Ships, Ferries and Cargo Vessels at Civitavecchia
intro: Civitavecchia is the sea gateway to Rome and one of the busiest cruise ports in the Mediterranean, with overnight ferries to Sardinia and Sicily, ro-ro lines and bulk berths alongside. Superintendents here work to short turnaround windows, so Atlantis NDT brings an inspection team from India to the ship and focuses on the spaces the schedule allows: scrubber piping, vehicle decks, ballast tanks and cargo holds.

highlights.h: Cruise turnaround is the working window
highlights.p: Large cruise ships spend a single day alongside between passengers leaving and boarding. That is enough for targeted gauging of scrubber lines, void spaces and items carried over from the last survey, if the scope is agreed beforehand.

highlights.h: Sardinia ferries return to the berth daily
highlights.p: Overnight ro-pax services to Olbia, Golfo Aranci and other Sardinian ports keep ships on a repeating cycle, so ramp, vehicle deck and tank readings can be built up over several calls.

highlights.h: Bulk and ro-ro work beside the passenger quays
highlights.p: Civitavecchia also handles dry bulk, project cargo and trailers, so the same visit can cover a bulk carrier's holds or a ro-ro ship's ramps in addition to passenger ships.

port.h: The port of Civitavecchia and its cruise, ferry and cargo traffic
p: Civitavecchia lies on the Lazio coast to the northwest of Rome and is the largest port in the Rome area. Its harbour is formed by long breakwaters, with the historic basin close to the town and newer outer quays built along the breakwater for the largest ships. Ships arrive directly from the open Tyrrhenian with no lock or tidal gate, so access is straightforward and the working day is set by the passenger programme rather than by water levels. Pilotage and tugs are provided as in other Italian ports, and anchorage is available outside the breakwater for ships waiting for a berth.

Cruise traffic dominates the summer calendar. Several of the world's biggest cruise lines turn ships round here, with passengers heading to Rome by road and rail, and the port often has more than one large ship alongside at the same time. A cruise ship spends only a day in Civitavecchia, but that day recurs every week through the season, which gives an owner a regular chance to look at the same areas on repeated calls. Alongside the cruise ships, ferries link the port with Sardinia, including Olbia, Golfo Aranci and Cagliari, and with Sicily, running overnight and returning to the berth the next day.

The commercial side of the port is smaller in the public eye but real. Dry bulk is discharged here to feed industrial and power customers on this stretch of the coast, ro-ro ships carry trailers to Spain and the islands, and forest products and project cargo pass through general cargo quays. The port belongs to a wider system that also includes Fiumicino and Gaeta, so owners can tie ships in neighbouring ports to the same visit. For thickness gauging, Civitavecchia is a port of short, well-planned windows rather than of long repair stays.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging is done in Civitavecchia
p: Civitavecchia is not known as a drydock port, and ships that need a full docking usually go to Naples, Palermo, Livorno or another Mediterranean yard. What the port does offer is a series of berths where a ship lies still for a known period. Cruise berths on the outer breakwater give the longest and most predictable turnaround for passenger ships, while the ferry quays near the historic harbour give repeating overnight cycles, and the cargo quays give the time between discharge and loading.

Because the work is done afloat, the key to a useful visit is a list of spaces agreed in advance with the superintendent and the chief engineer: which scrubber lines will be shut down, which voids the crew can ventilate, which ballast tanks can be emptied and certified gas-free, and which decks are clear of passengers or vehicles. Where a ship is laid up or waiting for a berth, a launch from the agent can take the team to the anchorage, though the weather window and the ship's readiness determine whether tank entry is practical. For ships heading to a yard, readings taken here set out the likely steel renewal before the docking is booked.
list: Outer breakwater cruise berths — turnaround-day gauging of scrubber wash-water lines, void spaces and previously noted structure on large cruise ships
Historic harbour ferry quays — vehicle deck, ramp and ballast tank readings on Sardinia and Sicily ro-pax ships over repeated visits
Ro-ro and trailer berths — ramp, hoistable car deck and stern door structure on ro-ro cargo ships between loading and sailing
Dry bulk berths — hold, tank-top and hatch cover gauging on carriers after discharge and cleaning
Roads outside the breakwater — owner's condition work on ships at anchor, in lay-up or waiting for a berth, with a launch arranged by the agent
Fiumicino and Gaeta — nearby ports in the same system that can be added to one mobilisation when the owner has ships there

context.h: Port state control, passenger-ship regimes and Rome's environmental rules
p: Foreign ships in Civitavecchia are subject to port state control under the Paris MoU, carried out by the Italian Coast Guard, the Guardia Costiera. Cruise ships and ferries in scheduled service also face the EU inspection regime for passenger ships, so structural defects on a Civitavecchia ferry are likely to be found soon. The port has also been active on air quality, since a large cruise ship at the quay burns fuel for hotel services for the whole stay; many ships here run exhaust gas cleaning systems or shore power where it is available, which is why scrubber piping is a frequent gauging target on passenger ships.

The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials for ships calling at EU ports, and owners often deal with it while planning a larger survey. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime now apply to the bigger passenger ships and ro-ro ships that call here, so the decision to renew steel or to replace tonnage is increasingly based on measured condition as well as on regulation. Cruise lines and Sardinian ferry operators both rely on a steady supply of up-to-date hull records, and the short turnaround at Civitavecchia means the data has to be gathered efficiently.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Civitavecchia
jobs.p: Most Civitavecchia jobs depend on a short fixed window. Cruise work means one ship, one day and a precisely chosen scope; ferry work means several short visits over a week or two; bulk and ro-ro work means the interval between discharge and sailing. We prepare the list of measurement points ahead of arrival, so the team can begin as soon as the ship is secured and access is cleared, and leave a consolidated record for the superintendent.
list: Wall-thickness survey of scrubber wash-water, overboard discharge and shell outlet piping on a cruise ship at its turnaround berth
Ballast tank and void space gauging on a cruise ship, concentrating on areas flagged in the last survey report
Ro-pax ferry vehicle deck, ramp and tank readings at Civitavecchia on a Sardinia service, built up across several calls ahead of a docking
Hold and hatch cover gauging on a dry bulk carrier after discharge at the commercial quay
Owner's condition check on a ro-ro ship at anchor outside the breakwater before a sale or charter change

logistics: Rome Fiumicino Airport is the nearest major gateway and is connected to Civitavecchia by road and a regional rail line; Rome Ciampino serves some European flights. The ship's agent arranges ISPS passes and a launch for ships at anchor, and cruise terminals set their own pass procedures, which the agent clears in advance. The team travels from India, so a Schengen visa is applied for as soon as the call is confirmed, and owners should factor the processing time into any plan for a cruise ship's single turnaround day.

faqs.q: How much can be gauged on a cruise ship in one turnaround day at Civitavecchia?
faqs.a: A defined block, not the whole ship. Scrubber piping, selected voids and a few ballast tanks are typical. The scope is agreed with the superintendent beforehand so the team starts at once and the results are ready for the surveyor. Larger programmes are spread over several weekly calls.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Civitavecchia for renewal survey work?
faqs.a: Civitavecchia is mainly a cruise, ferry and cargo port. Ships needing a docking normally go to a repair yard in Naples, Palermo, Livorno or elsewhere. We gauge at Civitavecchia beforehand to size the steel renewal and then follow the ship into dock, using the same reference points.

faqs.q: Can scrubber piping be gauged while the ship is in service?
faqs.a: Only where the system can be isolated and the pipework is accessible and safe to work near. On a cruise turnaround the scrubber is often shut down for part of the stay, which gives the time. We agree the lines and the shutdown period with the chief engineer in advance.

faqs.q: Do you work at Fiumicino or Gaeta as well as Civitavecchia?
faqs.a: Yes, both are in the same port system and reachable by road. If an owner has a ship at Civitavecchia and another in Fiumicino or Gaeta in the same week, we plan one mobilisation across the ports, based on each ship's schedule and the scope agreed with its superintendent.

faqs.q: What can be done for a ferry on a Sardinia route that is only in port overnight?
faqs.a: Overnight ferries are alongside for a limited time, so we take readings in blocks: a ramp, a deck section or a group of ballast tanks per visit. Over several calls this builds a full picture. We agree each visit's target with the superintendent and the master first.
